items.item_text: Experience working as a receptionist in a busy office environment including acting as first point of contact, performing general office procedures, and implementing and maintaining filing and records systems.
Experience working with visitors exercising professional, tactful, and diplomatic communication techniques. Experience working with databases maintaining large amounts of data – e.g. CRM’s.
Experience providing administrative support in complex, high-level executive offices.

Under general supervision, serves as the Career Services Coordinator and provides high-level administrative, analytical, and programmatic support for the School of Law Career Services Office and Externship Program. Independently manages a broad range of operational functions, including administration of the 12Twenty career management system, employer, alumni, and student databases, job and externship postings, reciprocity requests, office communications, records management, and recruitment-related activities. Serves as the primary point of contact for students, alumni, faculty, employers, and prospective students, exercising sound judgment and professionalism in responding to inquiries, applying established policies and procedures, and handling sensitive and confidential information.

Coordinates and supports employer recruitment programs, including virtual and on-campus interviewing, recruiting events, application collection processes, scheduling, event logistics, room reservations, and employer engagement activities. Provides comprehensive administrative support to the Director of Externships by managing student registration processes, tracking externship participation and compliance requirements, maintaining field placement information, and coordinating program events and communications. Collects, maintains, and analyzes program and operational data; prepares reports and recommendations; identifies process improvements; develops and updates administrative procedures; and contributes to program assessment, planning, and decision-making efforts. Collaborates effectively with Career Services staff, faculty, employers, alumni, students, and campus partners to ensure the effective delivery of career development, recruitment, and experiential education services.
Computer skills and knowledge of Microsoft Office Suite and its applications, Google Docs, and Box to create, format, and edit documents and spreadsheets containing data, graphs and tables.
Knowledge of UCD and School of Law instruction activities, policies and procedures.

Organizational skills to prioritize and complete multiple tasks in a busy environment under multiple deadlines. Writing, editing and proofreading skills to prepare letters, reports, and a variety of general correspondence.

Problem solving skills to develop creative solutions to general problems, initiative to attempt unfamiliar projects/assignments, and respond with flexibility to requests for assistance. Interpersonal, oral and written communication skills.
